chapter: Boston childhood, learning music and first gigs
title: Saxophonists had to own a clarinet; Buster Bailey's wooden clarinet
summary: Every saxophonist carried a Boehm clarinet because the stock parts called for it; Buster Bailey impressed him most in the 1925 Henderson band.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Reeds, mouthpieces and horns: the reed player's gear

blocks.x: Did you ever try to play a clarinet in Boston? Did you try out Carney's clarinet?
Sure, I had a clarinet!
You had a clarinet?
Sure. Everybody. All saxophone players had clarinets. Everyone couldn't play them. Most of them couldn't. But you had to have it.
[LAUGHS]

No, you had to have it. You had to have it because the parts called for it in music -- your stock music. Play two choruses and then they'd go into the clarinet chorus. Yeah, it's funny you had to have a clarinet. Coleman Hawkins had one...
Holmes (10/9) - 28
When did you get your first clarinet, then? Shortly after you got your saxophone?
Mmm, well, back in them days, yeah, because it went with the saxophone, you know. But I mean, I never cared for clarinet to play it. I just had it because I had to have it.
But you owned one in the end.
Yeah. It was a terrible thing to go on a job if you didn't have a clarinet.
Do you remember if it was Albert or Boehm system?
No, it was Boehm. Then when I come to New York, I bought a metal clarinet. It was a Boehm.
Now, Buster Bailey was playing a metal clarinet.
Yeah, he played one for years, sure.
So when you first saw him, he probably was on a metal, was he?
No, no.
He had a wood?

He had a wooden clarinet. When he came to Boston in '25, he was playing a wooden clarinet! And he could play it, too. He impressed me. He really did... He impressed me more than anybody in that band at that time. And Louis was there, and Coleman Hawkins was there...
Don Redman was there.
Holmes (10/9) - 29
Don Redman was there. But Buster impressed me more on that clarinet than anybody else in the band. But the whole band was impressive, though. Yeah, it was quite a band.
[END OF TAPE 1, SIDE 1]
